rows.text: Before the Second Great Prosperity, interstellar travel was an absolute slog. Limited by the technology of the time, ships often took months just to cross a star system, while long-distance voyages were measured in years. Many sailors would end up losing themselves in the boundless cosmos, succumbing to depression or delirium, even treating the control console as their best friend. To assist in crew psychological intervention, a Doctor of Chaos named Pino invented "Positive Emotion Hardtack." Consumers would recall the happiest moments of their lives, enabling them to do anything with a positive attitude. However, after its widespread adoption, many employees used it during performance reviews to derive happiness from working overtime. The IPC quickly banned the production of these hardtacks. Nowadays, people must rely on their own strength to confront the sense of desolate emptiness.
